steps.title: Harvest cells at confluence
steps.instruction: When cultures reach 70‑80 % confluence, aspirate the spent media and wash the monolayer twice with PBS.

steps.title: Add trypsin‑EDTA and incubate
steps.instruction: Add the appropriate trypsin‑EDTA (e.g., 0.1 % trypsin with 1 mM EDTA for U2OS cells) and incubate at 37 °C for the required time (1.5 min for U2OS; adjust for other lines).

steps.title: Inspect and release cells
steps.instruction: Examine the culture under a microscope; if cells have not rounded up, incubate an additional 1 min. Once rounded, tap or “smack” the flask/dish sides to aid detachment and immediately add complete growth media at 4 × the volume of trypsin added (e.g., 1 mL trypsin → 4 mL media). Use gentler taps for dishes to avoid spilling.

steps.title: Collect detached cells
steps.instruction: Using a 1 mL pipette, gently pipette (“blow”) any remaining cells off the surface, transfer the suspension to a 15 mL conical tube with a serological pipette, then add a few more milliliters of media to the flask/dish, swirl, and add this rinse to the same tube.

steps.title: Centrifuge or proceed to counting
steps.instruction: Decide whether to centrifuge the cell suspension. If centrifugation is needed, spin the tube for 5 min at 300 × g; otherwise proceed directly to cell counting.

steps.title: Resuspend cell pellet
steps.instruction: After centrifugation, aspirate the supernatant leaving ~100 µL to avoid disturbing the pellet, add fresh growth media (volume depends on harvest size), and resuspend vigorously with a 1 mL pipette.

steps.title: Break up clumps
steps.instruction: Using a serological pipette, pipette the suspension up and down 10–20 times to ensure a single‑cell suspension.

steps.title: Determine cell concentration
steps.instruction: Count cells (e.g., with a hemacytometer) to calculate cells / mL, then multiply by the total suspension volume to obtain the total harvested cell number. Optionally assess viability by counting trypan‑blue‑positive (dead) cells and dividing by total cells.

steps.title: Calculate seeding volume
steps.instruction: Using the desired seeding density, compute the volume of cell suspension needed. Example: for a 100 mm dish, if the suspension is 1 × 10⁶ cells/mL, pipette 0.5 mL (0.5 × 10⁶ cells) and add to 8 mL fresh media.

steps.title: Distribute cells evenly
steps.instruction: Seed the calculated volume and evenly distribute cells across the plate by moving the pipette tip in a north‑south then east‑west pattern.

steps.title: Prepare trypan‑blue sample
steps.instruction: Transfer 10 µL of the cell suspension to a sterile microcentrifuge tube, invert several times if the suspension has been standing, then add trypan blue: 10 µL for a 2× dilution (dilute cells), 40 µL for a 5× dilution, or 90 µL for a 10× dilution, depending on cell concentration.

steps.title: Load hemacytometer
steps.instruction: Mix the trypan‑blue‑cell mixture by flicking or pipetting, then load 8.5 µL onto the hemacytometer using a P200 pipette tip (the tip is attached to a P10 pipette to avoid clogging by larger cells). Count live and dead cells.
